annotations.annotation_text: Egyptian eschatology "Nuvoletta" on page 159 ("The Quiz Chapter"): within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones, HCE appears as the dismembered Osiris and ALP as Isis gathering his scattered limbs. Mark Troy's research traces how Joyce embedded the Papyrus of Ani's resurrection liturgy throughout this Age of Gods passage — the dream-journey through the underworld (Tuat) toward solar rebirth.

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 159 ("The Quiz Chapter"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. During this Age of Gods phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.

annotations.annotation_text: Mamalujo signal "waves" on page 159 ("The Quiz Chapter"): the Four Old Men — Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; Ulster, Munster, Leinster, Connaught — serve here as senile chroniclers and bedpost witnesses during twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. In this Age of Gods passage, they observe and record the dream's events as squawking gulls circling overhead.
